Title:
PERSA: Reinforcement Learning for Professor-Style Personalized Feedback with LLMs
Authors:
Ravi Ranjan
,
Utkarsh Grover
,
Xiaomin Lin
,
Agoritsa Polyzou
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) can provide automated feedback in educational settings, but aligning an LLMs style with a specific instructors tone while maintaining diagnostic correctness remains challenging. We ask how can we update an LLM for automated feedback generation to align with a target instructors style without sacrificing core knowledge? We study how Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) can adapt a transformer-based LLM to generate programming feedback that matches a professors grading voice. We introduce PERSA, an RLHF pipeline that combines supervised fine-tuning on professor demonstrations, reward modeling from pairwise preferences, and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), while deliberately constraining learning to style-bearing components. Motivated by analyses of transformer internals, PERSA applies parameter efficient fine-tuning. It updates only the top transformer blocks and their feed-forward projections, minimizing global parameter drift while increasing stylistic controllability. We evaluate our proposed approach on three code-feedback benchmarks (APPS, PyFiXV, and CodeReviewQA) using complementary metrics for style alignment and fidelity. Across both Llama-3 and Gemma-2 backbones, PERSA delivers the strongest professor-style transfer while retaining correctness, for example on APPS, it boosts Style Alignment Score (SAC) to 96.2% (from 34.8% for Base) with Correctness Accuracy (CA) up to 100% on Llama-3, and Gemma-2. Overall, PERSA offers a practical route to personalized educational feedback by aligning both what it says (content correctness) and, crucially, how it says it (instructor-like tone and structure).

Most common steps in such cycle involve- recognizing a problem, defining it, developing a strategy in order to fix it, organizing knowledge and resources available, monitoring progress, and evaluating the effectiveness of the solution. Once a solution is obtained, another problem usually comes, and the cycle starts again. Searching techniques in problem-solving by using artificial intelligence (A.I) are surveyed in this paper. An overview of definitions, development and dimensions of A.I in the light of search for solutions to problems are accepted. Dimensions as well as relevance of search in A.I research is reviewed. A classification of searching in the matter of depth of known parameters of search was also investigated. At last, the forethoughts of searching in AI research are brought into prominence. Search is noticed that it is the common thread that binds most of the problem-solving strategies in AI together.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.32628/ijsrset22962\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2022, 11, 1]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7610838\", \"title\": [\"Autonomous Thermal Engineering: Integration of Digital Twins, Artificial Intelligence, and Advanced Heat Transfer Mechanisms for Sustainable Energy Systems\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Thermal engineering systems are increasingly facing challenges associated with dynamic operating conditions, energy efficiency demands, and the transition toward sustainable energy infrastructures. This study presents an autonomous thermal engineering framework that integrates digital twins, artificial intelligence (AI), and advanced heat transfer mechanisms to enhance the performance, reliability, and adaptability of next-generation energy systems. The proposed framework combines real-time sensing, physics-based thermal modelling, machine learning algorithms, and intelligent optimization strategies to continuously monitor, predict, and regulate thermal behaviour. The digital twin establishes a virtual representation of physical thermal systems, enabling accurate simulation, fault prediction, and autonomous decision-making under varying environmental and operational conditions. AI-driven models improve thermal management by learning complex nonlinear relationships between operating parameters, heat transfer characteristics, and system performance indicators. Advanced heat transfer technologies, including enhanced convection, phase-change materials, nanofluids, and adaptive thermal control mechanisms, support improved heat dissipation and energy utilization. The integrated approach provides a self-optimizing thermal architecture that reduces energy losses, increases system efficiency, and promotes sustainable operation. The framework demonstrates significant potential for applications in renewable energy systems, industrial thermal processes, electric mobility, and smart energy networks. This research establishes a pathway toward autonomous, intelligent, and environmentally responsible thermal engineering solutions for future energy systems.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7610838\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1109/aiars63200.2024.00024\", \"title\": [\"Research on the Selection of Road Guidance Sign Information in Chinese Cities\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1109/aiars63200.2024.00024\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2024, 7, 29]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "5edb31b7d9734c8c4829a804fc9e28dd89056b4aa551e34a30d380d10bf04e1c", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "unassigned_problem", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.1016/j.engappai.2022.104661", "doi:10.32628/ijsrset22962", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.7610838", "doi:10.1109/aiars63200.2024.00024"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.1016/j.engappai.2022.104661", "https://doi.org/10.32628/ijsrset22962", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7610838", "https://doi.org/10.1109/aiars63200.2024.00024"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
